text:
As of 2020, Sub-Saharan Africa’s average real income per person was above its 1980 level: it fell into the mid-1990s, then rose for about twenty-five years, and the 2020 pandemic dip left the regional average still higher than in 1980. Congo (the DRC) really did have real income per person in 2020 far below its 1980 level, and that collapse is one severe country path inside the average. The regional record is the combined path of many economies, above all Nigeria, Ethiopia, South Africa, Kenya, and Tanzania.

CONFIDENCE: 76
